verdict.rationale: Granola documents an official MCP server that connects Claude, ChatGPT and other AI tools to your meeting notes, letting them query notes, search transcripts and find topics from past meetings. A community user confirms it takes "a couple of clicks to setup with Claude/ChatGPT," which supports the no-glue-code claim. missing for 10: explicit documentation of OAuth as the MCP auth method, and evidence that action items are exposed through the MCP tools rather than only via the REST API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an official MCP server lets Claude or any MCP client query my meetings — search, transcripts, action items — with OAuth, no glue code

citations.quote: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI tools to your Granola meeting notes via MCP. Query your notes, search transcripts, and get meeting insights in your favorite AI assistants.
Once connected you can use this to: search through your meeting notes, find specific topics discussed in past meetings
a MCP that is a couple of clicks to setup with Claude/ChatGPT
